Container.Name: NexCraft-Daemon
Container.Overview:
The NexCraft daemon — the per-node agent that actually runs your Minecraft servers (downloads modpacks, bootstraps loaders, provisions Java, runs the processes). Pair it with the NexCraft-Web (panel) container.
Ships with Java 21 and auto-provisions other JRE versions per pack. After it's running, add it as a node in the NexCraft panel (default port 24444) using the access key from its data/Config/global.json. The Docker socket mount is optional and only needed for the (legacy) Docker-instance mode; host/general process mode does not require it. Docs: https://dpavlakis.github.io/NexCraft/
Container.Requires: Install the NexCraft-Web container too — it's the dashboard that connects to this daemon.

Config.Name: Daemon Port
Config.Description: Daemon RPC port the panel connects to.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Daemon data: instances, configs, the access key and (with the backup mount below) backups.

Config.Name: Backups
Config.Description: Where instance backups are stored. Point this at a dedicated share (e.g. /mnt/user/Backup/Minecraft) to keep backups off appdata, or leave it under the Data path if you prefer. Clear the field to keep backups inside the Data volume.

Config.Name: Instance Data Host Path
Config.Description: Host path to the InstanceData folder (used only by the legacy Docker-instance mode; harmless otherwise). Keep it pointing at <Data path>/InstanceData.

Config.Name: Docker Socket (optional)
Config.Description: Optional: only needed for legacy Docker-instance mode. Host/general process mode does not need it.
